newsitem.title: UK: London gold bid below $337.15, first time since '9.
newsitem.headline: London gold bid below $337.15, first time since '9.

text.p: Gold was indicated in Europe at $336.50/$337.00 per ounce for the first time since mid-April 1993 on Wednesday.

The fall from Tuesday's close of $339.30/$339.80 reflected renewed strength in the U.S. dollar which rose to a 34-month high against the mark and came close to topping its recent four-year peak against the yen.
The most recent price slide began in New York on Tuesday when the dollar began to gain ground against the other major trading currencies.
The surge in the foreign exchange markets effectively ended any hopes that low gold price would attract fresh investment and provoked fresh selling of gold
"Sentiment remains extremely bearish. Apart from corrective bounces, the market remains locked in a downtrend," one dealer said.

The threat of selling from central bank vaults as gold's role as a reserve asset is re-assessed plus selling into the market by gold producers have kept the gold price under pressure since the middle of last year.
